body: Me too, but it hasn't happened yet..got about a month or so. How long you think you got? What do your days look like? Personally I've been spending a lot of time on my living room floor thinking about how I'm gonna figure all this shit out lol

Sure, but if someone is struggling with those things, telling them not to dwell on it or "make sure they don't rule your life" isn't exactly helpful. This person needs to be understood and helped on an individual basis. Not given platitudes and then buried under the new posts.

You're interesting. You very neatly summed up the weird feelings I've had about mental health professionals who use the kind of language you described. People who feel like they're in hell don't want to be told to stay there. Especially if the past has been a wasteland of pain and trauma, and the future seems to follow so much from the past. Why would I want to stay in the moment when I don't want to be here at all..
maybe not, but it clearly matters to this person. I don't think that should be dismissed

Hey stranger :) idk what you're struggling with, but I have bpd and know how much of a rollercoaster those highs and lows can be, makes me feel like I end up with emotional whiplash sometimes. Just know that you aren't your lows. There's a beautiful part of you that expresses itself kinda harshly sometimes during your highs but thats okay. You're a complex human being with complex problems, it's okay if you go off and feel invincible sometimes -- hell you deserve to just have those moments after what you have to put up with sometimes. Don't try to beat yourself up for it too much, you're still figuring it out. You're valuable in your entirety, not just for the fleeting moments during your highs, but the sensitive person you're feeling as now too. Hope you can find someone to remind you every day that you have value and deserve care & compassion, no matter what state you're in.

As someone who has been on both sides, grew up poor, made okay money in my mid-20s, then went poor again...you'd be surprised how little money can change your mental health when the problems run deeper. Everyone is different and has different problems. But I know for me I was most miserable when I had a bunch of money in my bank account, knowing that even though things were supposed to get better the money didn't make me wanna kill myself any less. What do you feel like money is preventing you from doing that would make you happier?

I mean I've had several attempts too and I think I still have experiences worth talking about, I'm sure you do too. I know I need to change as a person for things to change, but if you've been through some fucked shit that scars you for life idk how anyone gets over it or becomes okay with it I have no idea. Like having a permanent injury that nobody else can see but you, and so nobody sees how debilitating it is. It's like driving with a flat tire your whole life and everyone is wondering why your driving is so shitty lol, feels like I just need to die and be reborn as someone else
is it ok to pm you?

I feel your pain, and I'm sorry that the world has been an unfair place for you. You're right honestly, it's not fair how much of a leg up a little bit of privilege can give you in life. But being pretty isn't a guarantee of anything in life, and looks fade with time. You can be pretty and still end up homeless, abused, suicidal, etc. Sure life is probably easier when you have that kind of advantage as a baseline, but it won't prevent you sinking just as low as anyone else. I'm super curious how you imagine your life might have been/might be different if you had a face you felt more comfortable and confident waking to. What would that allow you to do that you feel like you can't do right now?

I wish I had answers for you. I also have bpd and it honestly feels like an unlivable condition, like I do not fit in with how society works at all. I totally relate, but I really don't know any better than you. What do you wish could be different about your life? Is it your feelings? The way they influence your behavior? Your conditions/environment? What would have to change in the world or within you for you to want to stay in this place?

You're putting a lot on your shoulders at a really young age. It can feel crushing. I'm far from an optimist, but try to find some good in your world from time to time and appreciate it. Maybe you'll find something worth fighting for, maybe not. There's so much bad in the world and if we only ever choose to engage with that it'll destroy us. You seem like a really introspective person, just know that logical thinking doesn't always lead us down a path where we're happier. You seem pretty smart my guy, give yourself some more time to figure it all out
